title: An ample invertible sheaf realizes a scheme as an open subscheme of Proj
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with an ample invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ [def-sc-invertible-module] [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then there exist a nonnegatively graded commutative ring $S$ and an open immersion $X\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-pc-proj].

source.place: Properties Proposition 01Q3 (properties-proposition-characterize-ample), implication (1) => (2), with S = Gamma_*(X, L)

proof.text: Form the nonnegatively graded section ring $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$. By [lem-sc-ample-finite-affine-cover] choose finitely many positive-degree homogeneous sections $s_i$ with affine principal opens $X_{s_i}$ covering $X$; hence the cover hypothesis of [lem-sc-ample-proj-local-chart] holds, and that node provides the canonical morphism $f:X\to\operatorname{Proj}(S)$.

source.place: Properties Proposition 01Q3, implication (1) => (2), Lemma 01PZ, and Lemma 01Q1 proof, first paragraph

proof.text: For each $i$, [lem-sc-ample-proj-local-chart] gives $f^{-1}(D_+(s_i))=X_{s_i}$ and, because $X_{s_i}$ is affine, identifies $X_{s_i}\to D_+(s_i)$ as an isomorphism. Thus the image of $f$ is the union of the open standard charts $D_+(s_i)$, and $f$ is an isomorphism over each of them.

source.place: Properties Lemma 01Q1 proof, paragraphs beginning 'The inverse image of D_+(s_i)' and 'By Lemma 01PW'

proof.text: The local isomorphisms in step 2 agree on overlaps because they are restrictions of the single canonical morphism $f$. They therefore identify $X$ with the open subscheme $\bigcup_iD_+(s_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Proj}(S)$, so $f$ is an open immersion.

source.place: Properties Lemma 01Q1 proof, final two sentences
